summary: _“(a) To take on record of the details and prayers as submitted by the Petitioner through this affidavit;_ _(b) Declare and hold that imposition of Mineral Bearing Land Tax which has resulted in increase in input price of Lignite and consequent energy charges of the Petitioner as a change in law;_ _(c) Permit the Petitioner to bill the Tax paid as “Statutory Charges” in the input price of lignite and recover the same from its beneficiaries through landed cost of lignite as energy charge component of tariff of linked Thermal Stations;_ _(d) To grant the interim relief for recovery of the same through monthly billing till issue of the final order;_ _(e) To grant carrying cost if there is any difference between the date of payment of the tax by the Petitioner and its recovery from the beneficiaries at the rate of interest applicable as per Tariff regulations 2024-29 for the Tariff difference;_ - (d) The Petitioner has executed various Power Purchase Agreements (“PPAs”) with the Respondents governing the sale and supply of electricity generated from its thermal power stations. These PPAs contain provisions enabling it to recover the statutory charges payable by the Petitioner. The imposition of land tax constitutes a change in law and has a direct impact on the charges payable by the Petitioner. This has resulted in an increase in the landed cost of lignite, and consequently, the energy charges for NLCIL's thermal stations - (k) The petition is filed at the earliest instance, following the enactment and notification of the 2024 Act and the subsequent Rules, which came into effect from 4.4.2025. The Petition is filed within three years from the date of levy and is therefore within the limitation period. 5. During the hearing on 18.9.2025, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present petition has been filed for in-principle approval for claiming Land Tax payable under the 2024 Act, as a statutory charge, and for recovery of the same through the Input Price of Lignite of Neyveli Mines from DISCOMs of linked thermal stations. The Commission, after hearing the learned counsel for Petitioner, admitted the Petition and issued notice to the parties. Further, the Respondents were directed to file their reply on or before 31.10.2025, and the Petitioner to file its rejoinder, if any, by 14.11.2025. Reply has been filed by the TANGEDCO, Respondent No.1, vide affidavit dated 26.11.2025 and the Petitioner has filed its rejoinder to the reply filed by TANGEDCO, vide affidavit dated 12.12.2025. - (a) While allowing any compensation on account of the levy of Land Tax as a change in law event, the interests of the Respondents may be safeguarded. - (c) The Petitioner has to submit detailed and duly audited computations along with its monthly regular or supplementary bills of change in law claims and also furnish monthly details of tax actually paid, along with the required halfyearly and annual statutory returns, to enable proper verification and reconciliation of the claims. - (d) Any penalty, interest, or additional liability arising due to disputes or noncompliance by the Petitioner with the concerned statutory authority should not be allowed as a pass-through to the Respondents, and any excess amount recovered by the Petitioner, whether on account of advance estimation or otherwise, must be refunded to the Respondents along with applicable interest. 7. During the hearing on 27.11.2025, the learned counsel for the Petitioner sought time to file its rejoinder in the matter. However, the learned counsel for the Petitioner and Respondent, TNPDCL, submitted that the Commission may reserve its order in the matter. The Commission, after hearing the parties, directed the Petitioner to file its rejoinder on or before 12.12.2025, after serving a copy on the Respondent. Subject to the above, the order in the petition was reserved. 8. The Petitioner, in its rejoinder to the reply filed by TANGEDCO vide affidavit dated 12.12.2025, has made the following submissions: made by the Petitioner. TANGEDCO has further submitted that any penalty, interest, or additional liability arising due to disputes or non-compliance should not be allowed as a pass through. TANGEDCO has also submitted that the relief should be limited to _(b) adoption, amendment, modification, repeal or re-enactment of any existing Indian law; or_ _(c) change in interpretation or application of any Indian law by a competent court, Tribunal or Indian Governmental Instrumentality which is the final authority under law for such interpretation or application; or_ _(e) coming into force or change in any bilateral or multilateral agreement or treaty between the Government of India and any other Sovereign Government having implications for the generating station or the transmission system regulated under these regulations.”_ 24. The Petitioner has also sought carrying cost, if there is any difference between the date of payment of the tax by the Petitioner and its recovery from the beneficiaries, as per the 2024 Tariff Regulations for the difference in the tariff. 25. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner regarding carrying cost, and we are of the view that it is premature and hence it is not allowed in this order. - (d) The Petitioner is allowed to provisionally bill the Land Tax paid, as “Statutory Charges”, in monthly energy charge bills pending final determination, subject to reconciliation at the time of truing up. - (e) The Petitioner’s prayer for carrying cost in case of delay in payment of the Land Tax by the beneficiaries is premature, and it is not allowed in this order. The Petitioner may raise the same, along with the details in its petition for approval of tariff for the 2024-24 tariff period, as advised, for consideration by the Commission.
